title: Day-by-day navigation, a random reading link, and no future dates

history.detail:
FAIL: FAIL, gate 1, audit of e444619. One requirement is not met: R6 as amended. That also leaves R10 short.

Sprint file: read fresh. R6 was amended in 9dc8580 at 09:42 (-0500), after /sprint-start (5df44d2, 09:28) and before the audited commit. git diff 9dc8580 e444619 -- docs/sprints/ is empty, so the audited commit was built against the amended file. The build implements the PRE-amendment R6.

DEFECT, R6 phone amendment, demonstrated:
- Required: at 900px and below, the random link and its "or" are NOT on the picker row. The link appears after the reading section, directly above Other notable dates, using one server-side pick shared by both copies, with a test showing both hrefs equal.
- At e444619, app/date/[date]/DatePicker.tsx renders the link and its "or" unconditionally inside .pickerControls, with no layout class.
- grep for mobileOnly or desktopOnly in DatePicker.tsx and page.tsx exits 1.
- page.tsx passes afterBody only NotableDatesSection, so there is no bottom copy.
- Dev Team's own handoff measurement confirms it at 390: "Go and 'or' share a line, and DISCOVER RANDOM READING wraps onto the next", meaning it is on the picker row on phones.
- No test covers two copies or a shared href.

R10 is short as a direct consequence. The amended sprint asks for a phone shot of the bottom (reading, random link, notable dates) and a phone shot of the top showing the picker row with no random link. Neither exists. phone-390-random-link-wrapped.png shows the old layout.

Required to clear this FAIL:
(1) At 900px and below, hide the picker-row link and its "or". Render the link after the reading section and before NotableDatesSection, outside the reading section's sticky container. Use the same randomDate the page already computes once.
(2) Add a test that both copies carry the same href, and that the bottom copy is placed between the reading section and the notable-dates section.
(3) Add a Round 2 handoff section with the two phone screenshots. Include a check that the sticky reveal bar does not cover the bottom link when a horoscope is folded (LiveQA step 6 will check this too).

Everything else checks out. I'd expect it to stand on re-audit unless the fix touches it.
- R1 Met. isAfterToday in lib/date-page/params.ts is the single comparison. Its boundary tests use an injected now.
- R2 Met. The page test shows a 307 to today with zero RPCs, so the redirect comes before loadDatePage. Invalid and out-of-range dates still 404 on both routes.
- R3 Met. max is today, computed per request, and a test reads it.
- R4 Met. Both write paths are covered by tests. Dev Team's question 2: refusing after get_reading_by_id, before the admin client and OpenAI, is the right placement. The stored event_date is needed and nothing is written first.
- R5 Met. The arithmetic tests include every required case, plus century and minimum-date cases. Previous day is absent on 1700-01-01. Both day links render with lookups paused.
  Dev Team's question 1: a span with role link, aria-disabled true, no href and no tabindex is acceptable. It's the standard disabled-link pattern: it is not navigable and not focusable, and a screen reader announces it as dimmed. A role-less span would have aria-disabled ignored.
- R6, except the phone amendment: the pure pick is tested with a fixed random source, and excludes the page's own date and the future. Lookup failure and an empty pool render nothing. The link reuses .pickerButton plus a two-property .pickerLink, not a copy.
- R7 Met. The grep exits 1, and supabase/migrations is unchanged.
- R8 and R9 Met as far as read. The README paragraph is accurate for the code, but must be re-checked once the phone layout changes.

My own check: npm run verify at e444619, on a clean tree. Result: verify=0, VERIFY PASS exit=0, 48 test files and 561 tests passed.

UNOWNED, routed to Master Controller: lint passes with 3 no-unused-expressions warnings, in docs/handoffs/sprint-45/cdp45.mjs, sprint-45/cdp45-overflow.mjs and sprint-46/cdp46.mjs. They are probe scripts from closed sprints. No decision to accept them is on record. I missed them in my own sprint 45 and 46 audits, because I read the exit code and the counts, not the warnings. Master Controller decides whether to clean them up or accept them on record. They don't fail lint, so they are not part of this FAIL.

PASS: PASS, gate 1 round 2, audit of 7b65d17. All three required fixes from round 1 are made.

Sprint file: re-read fresh. Unchanged since the R6 amendment (git diff 9dc8580 7b65d17 on the sprint file is empty).

Handoff: read at the audited commit. A Round 2 section was added; Round 1 is untouched (no deleted lines in the handoff diff). It quotes VERIFY PASS (lint, typecheck, test, build) exit=0, with 563 tests. It names the cause plainly: no re-read of the sprint file before handing off.

My own check: npm run verify at 7b65d17, on a clean tree. Result: verify=0, VERIFY PASS exit=0, 48 test files and 563 tests passed.

Fix 1, the R6 phone amendment: Met.
- RandomReading.tsx holds one link component, RandomReadingLink: Go's pickerButton class plus pickerLink, so the styles are reused, not copied.
- DatePicker wraps the "or" and the link in a span with the desktopOnly class. At 900px and below, desktopOnly is display none (reading.module.css, around line 568). So at phone widths the picker row is just the date input and Go.
- page.tsx passes afterBody as RandomReadingSection (mobileOnly) followed by NotableDatesSection. afterBody renders after the body div, outside the reading section and its sticky reveal.
- randomDate is computed once and passed to both copies. There is no second pick and no second lookup.
- No display is set on the new classes, so desktopOnly and mobileOnly own it, matching the existing dateNav convention.

Fix 2, tests: Met.
- The page test renders the real DatePage with Math.random fixed. It asserts exactly two link copies with an identical href, that the picker-row copy sits in pickerRandom desktopOnly together with its "or", and that the markup order is: section close, column close, body close, randomSection mobileOnly, notableSection.
- A no-date test asserts that neither copy renders.

Fix 3, R10 screenshots: Met. I opened all four round2 PNGs.
- Phone top: the picker row is ANOTHER DATE, the date and GO, with no "or" and no link. Previous day / Next day follow, then the chart tabs.
- Phone bottom: the folded reading section ("Reveal the horoscope"), then DISCOVER RANDOM READING, ruled off, then Other notable dates.
- Desktop 1280: GO, then OR, then DISCOVER RANDOM READING on the picker row, with day links for 19 and 21 July 1969.
- Desktop today: Next day is greyed, with "Reloy predicts only the past." visible in the date's place.
The sticky-bar check in round2-report.json shows 0px overlap and the link hit by elementFromPoint at five scroll offsets.

R9: the README paragraph is updated for the phone placement and the shared pick, and is accurate to the code.

Unchanged and still Met from round 1: R1 to R5, R7 (grep exit 1, migrations unchanged) and R8, plus my rulings on Dev Team's two round 1 questions.

Still UNOWNED, routed to Master Controller in round 1: lint's 3 no-unused-expressions warnings, in probe scripts from closed sprints 45 and 46. No decision is on record yet. Not this sprint's code, and lint exits 0.

For LiveQA: the disabled "Next day" label is deliberately faint; the visible message carries the meaning. Judge its contrast on the real device.
commit=7b65d17 | ci=green: 1 CI run(s) for 7b65d174aef3ab20d712debc2e6977f3c4d037d4 all completed successfully with real steps executed.

PASS: PASS (round 1). LiveQA steps 1 to 6 all pass on production. No defects. One observation for the user on step 3's contrast, below.

Tested 2026-11-25, about 15:17 to 15:40 UTC, against https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app. Today (UTC) was 2026-11-25, tomorrow 2026-11-26.
Shipped commit 7b65d17. Production serves the pushed tip 67cf3b1: /api/health/db reports status ok, connected true, commit 67cf3b1, with migrationVersion unchanged at 20261122152710_navigation_exact_date_readings. git diff --stat 7b65d17 origin/main touches only docs/sprints/state/sprint-47.json.
Tools: curl; headless Chromium (Playwright 1.57) at 1280x1000, and at 390x844 (isMobile, hasTouch) with JS on and off.

STEP 1, redirects: PASS. curl -sI at 15:17:07-15:17:09 UTC (response date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 15:17:07 GMT):
- /date/2026-11-26: HTTP/2 307, location /date/2026-11-25.
- /date?date=2026-11-26: 307, location /date/2026-11-25.
- Also /date/2027-01-01, /date?date=2100-12-31 and /date/2026-11-26?x=1: 307 to /date/2026-11-25.
- /date/2101-01-01: 404. /date/2024-02-30: 404. /date?date=2101-01-01 and /date?date=2024-02-30: 404 (15:20:57 UTC).
- Controls: /date/2026-11-25 200, /date/1969-07-20 200, /date?date=1969-07-20 307 to /date/1969-07-20, / 307 to /date/2026-11-25.
- Every response has cache-control "private, no-cache, no-store, max-age=0, must-revalidate".

STEP 2, day links: PASS.
- /date/1969-07-20: prev "← PREVIOUS DAY 19 July 1969" to /date/1969-07-19; next "NEXT DAY → 21 July 1969" to /date/1969-07-21. Clicking each lands there (h1 "19 July 1969", "21 July 1969"). Nav aria-label "Previous and next day".
- Calendar edges on production: 2000-02-28 next 2000-02-29; 2001-02-28 next 2001-03-01; 1999-12-31 next 2000-01-01; 2000-03-01 prev 2000-02-29.
- /date/1700-01-01: no Previous day link; Next day to /date/1700-01-02.
- No "Previous reading" or "Next reading" anywhere on these pages.
- Screenshot: s47-1280-1969.png.

STEP 3, today's page /date/2026-11-25: PASS.
- Previous day goes to /date/2026-11-24. No rel=next link.
- Next day is a SPAN with aria-disabled="true", no href, no tabindex, cursor default. Its text: "NEXT DAY → Reloy predicts only the past."
- The message "Reloy predicts only the past." is visible text (a SPAN, 15px), not a tooltip.
- A forced click on the disabled element left the URL at /date/2026-11-25. Tabbing through the page never focused it.
- Screenshots: s47-1280-today.png, s47-today-disabled-zoom.png.
- Contrast, measured on the canvas: the "Next day →" label is rgb(43,42,53) on rgb(9,9,15), 1.40:1 at 9.5px; the message is rgb(127,127,137) on the same background, 5.01:1 at 15px. The label is barely visible, which reads as disabled, and the message carries the meaning, as QA1 noted. WCAG's text-contrast rule exempts inactive controls, so this is not recorded as a defect. Judged from headless screenshots, not a physical device.

STEP 4, picker: PASS. On today's page, the date input has min "1700-01-01" and max "2026-11-25". Setting 2026-11-26 gives validity.rangeOverflow true and form.checkValidity() false; 2026-11-25 is valid. Typing 2026-11-26 and clicking Go does not submit: the URL stays /date/2026-11-25 and the browser message is "Value must be 11/25/2026 or earlier." Max was also 2026-11-25 on every other date page tested. The browser's own calendar popup can't be opened headless; the max attribute and validation are what restrict it.

STEP 5, Discover random reading: PASS.
- Five loads of /date/1969-07-20: /date/1971-11-24, /date/2008-09-15, /date/1920-08-19, /date/1918-11-11, /date/2004-12-26 (5 distinct).
- Five loads of /date/2026-11-25: /date/1939-09-01, /date/1991-11-07, /date/1939-09-01, /date/2023-05-06, /date/1991-11-07 (3 distinct).
- Never the page's own date and never after today, across these and all the other loads in this test (about 25 more).
- Each target I opened (1971-11-24, 2008-09-15, 1920-08-19, 2004-12-26, 2023-05-06, 1991-11-07, 2009-11-23, 2021-01-06) has a saved horoscope: "Revealed on request" is in the page, status "this exact date".
- Clicking the link on /date/1969-07-20 went to /date/2009-11-23, a saved reading.
- Both copies in the page carry the same href on every load checked (one is hidden by layout).

STEP 6, layout: PASS.
- 390px, on /date/1969-07-20, /date/2026-11-25 and the redirects from /date/2026-12-16 and /date/2031-05-09:
  - The picker row reads "ANOTHER DATE GO", with no visible random link. scrollWidth 390.
  - The order down the page (y on 1969-07-20) is: picker 211, Previous day / Next day 275, chart tabs 320, reading section 880-1149, Discover random reading 1168, "Other notable dates" 1239. The link is outside the reading section. The same order holds with the no-events message.
  - Tapping the link navigates to its target.
  - With JS off: scrollWidth 390, one visible link.
- Folded horoscope, 390px, on /date/1912-04-15 and /date/1969-09-01 (saved readings, showing "NOT REVEALED YET" with "REVEAL THE HOROSCOPE"):
  - With the link scrolled to y = 100, 400, 700, 760, 780, 800, 820 and 840 px, elementFromPoint at the link's centre always returned the link.
  - The sticky reveal bar always ended above the reading section's bottom, which is above the link.
  - Screenshots s47-390-1912-04-15-off780.png and s47-390-1969-09-01-off700.png / -off800.png show the link fully visible below the reveal bar.
  - One probe point at the very last pixel row (y 843 of 844) on 1969-09-01, with the link 4px into view, did not hit the link. Centre samples did, and the screenshots show no overlap. Not a defect.
- 1280px, on the same four pages: the link is on the picker row after Go, reading "ANOTHER DATE GO OR DISCOVER RANDOM READING"; it's the only visible copy, and there's none at the bottom. Screenshot: s47-1280-row.png.
- Go-button style, read with the mouse away from both. Go and the link compute identically at rest, on hover and on focus: border 1px solid, IBM Plex Mono 10.5px weight 400, uppercase, letter-spacing 1.89px, padding 9px 16px, the same text and border colours in each state, and on focus an outline of rgb(16,16,16) auto 1px. Both are 34px tall on the same row.

Everything else, spot-checked: the banner, Sprint 45's notable list (20 entries) and Sprint 39's no-events message render. 0 console or page errors across every run.
